A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 37-page versions of the same Partial Model Collapse paper. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original unlearning experiments, attack evaluations and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A, plus categorical and Gaussian-mixture simulations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the TOFU comparisons, utility evaluations in Table 1, MUSE-news results in Figure 29 and Appendix C simulations.

M1.justification: The PMC objective and Algorithm 1, preference-selection implementation, PMC-fast approximation and MUSE sentence-continuation adaptation are unchanged. The reward ablation already appears in v4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TOFU coverage, derived multiple-choice questions, wikitext, ARC/MMLU utility benchmarks, MUSE-news subset and categorical/Gaussian-mixture simulations. The sampling and prefilling scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The TOFU comparisons retain GA, GD, DPO, NPO, SimNPO and IDK, with the same Gemma-specific exclusions of DPO/NPO. Comparator membership also matches within the attack, side-effect and MUSE-news experiments.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, model configurations and experimental settings are unchanged. Figures 27–28 lose erroneous references to 10 epochs, but both versions already show 20 epochs in the plots and specify 20 in Appendix B.4; the captions are reconciled with the existing protocol.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter, runtime, attack, reward-convergence, reward-function and gradient-checkpointing analyses test the same questions with the same evidence. The revised captions for Figures 26–28 describe analyses already present in v4.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting, means and standard deviations, and the stated single-run exceptions remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A–B. No uncertainty estimation or reporting practice is added or removed.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1 and 3 and the plotted results retain the same values, trends and comparisons. In particular, Figures 26–28 contain unchanged curves despite their corrected captions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemma 1, Theorems 1–2, assumptions and derivations are unchanged, including the categorical-distribution and convergence proofs in Appendices C–D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about collapse-based unlearning, independence from ground-truth forget answers, theoretical convergence, utility preservation and robustness.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A.7 calls further judge-model validation 'important' instead of 'interesting', but both versions already state its necessity and retain the same tentative conclusion about self-BLEU rewards.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hyperparameters, hardware, sampling procedures, dataset-construction prompts and implementation details. Code/configuration access statements and the project-page address are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and the paper's positioning relative to prior unlearning and model-collapse research are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: There are small wording edits in Section 5.2 and Appendix A.7, including 'rather' becoming 'instead' and a shortened sentence about further validation. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 26's caption now identifies reward functions evaluated by epoch. Figures 27–28 correctly identify gradient-checkpointing ablations, replacing runtime/λ descriptions and removing erroneous 10-epoch statements. Figure 2 also changes initial-panel label bolding; plots, tables and their placement otherwise remain stable.

improvement.justification: v5 improves reporting clarity by correcting Figures 26–28's misleading captions to match their existing axes, legends and Appendix B.4 settings. This resolves concrete inconsistencies about the analyses and epoch counts. The methods, evidence, theory and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
